hints.title: At Most Twice Frequency Retention
hints.text: Each unique element may appear at most twice in the modified array. How can comparing the incoming element with the element placed two positions prior decide whether to write it?

hints.title: Two-Back Distance Comparison Invariant
hints.text: An element nums[i] is eligible to be written at write index k if k is less than two or nums[i] exceeds nums[k - 2].

hints.title: Slow Write Index Advancement Procedure
hints.text: Initialize write index k to 0. Iterate through each number in the array. If k is less than 2 or current number is strictly greater than nums[k - 2], write the current number to nums[k] and increment k. Return k as the new length.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Shifting array elements upon discovering duplicate counts requires O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Fast-slow pointer writing runs in O(N) time with O(1) in-place auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that comparing with nums[k - 2] cleanly generalizes to allowing at most k duplicates.
